summary: James Burnell Robinson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Richard Hugh Robinson (~1967–1970) and advisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa (~1968–1975). He became Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Northern Iowa (~1975).

James C. Dobbins works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Yale University in 1984 and served as Fairchild Professor of Religion and East Asian Studies at Oberlin College (attested 2015–2019).

James Charles Colebrooke Sutherland (1792–1844) worked in Indology and law. He studied at East India Company College, Fort William College, and under Thomas Roebuck, later serving as professor of law at Presidency University.

James Darmesteter (1849–1894) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Michel Bréal (~1872–1877) and held posts at the EPHE (~1877–1894) and Collège de France (1885–1894).

James Duerlinger works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1961–1964) and under Sheldon Pollock, later serving on the faculty at the University of Iowa (~1971–2012).
James Dwight Dana (1813–1895) studied at Yale College (~1830–1833) and held a post at Yale University (~1850–1892).

James Fergusson (1808–1886) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. In 1840, he was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland.
James Fieser is a scholar in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Berea College (~1976–1980) and Purdue University (~1983–1986), and held a post at the University of Tennessee (~1992).
James G. Mullens is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Gibbs (1825–1886) was an Indology and history/archaeology specialist. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1870–1879) and President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1876–1881).

James H. Austin is a Buddhist studies scholar and neurologist. He studied under Nanrei Sohaku Kobori, Kyozan Joshu Sasaki, and Katsujo Terayama, and held posts at OHSU, the University of Oregon, and the University of Colorado (~1965–1992).

James Hadley (1821–1872) studied at Yale under Edward Elbridge Salisbury. A linguist and Indologist, he was a tutor at Middlebury College (1845), Professor of Greek at Yale (1845–1872), and a leading officer of the American Oriental Society (1871–1872).

James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and religion. Educated at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Arthur Venis, Mukunda Shastri Adkar, and Charles Rockwell Lanman, he held a post at Harvard in 1914.

James Irving Manatt (1845–1915), a scholar of linguistics and archaeology, studied at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1884–1889), and Brown University (~1893–1915).

James Ishmael Ford works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned degrees from Sonoma State and Pacific School of Religion and studied under Sojun Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant, founding Boundless Way Zen and Empty Moon Zen Network.

James Kenneth Powell II is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Northwestern, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, 1998) under David Tracy, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen. He served as professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and Brown University (attested 2019).

James Legge (1815–1897) was a sinologist who studied at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1831–1835), and Highbury College. He was appointed Professor at the University of Oxford in 1876.

James Luther Adams (1901–1994) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, where he later held a post from ~1956 to 1968.

James Mackintosh (1765–1832) worked in history, archaeology, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and University of Edinburgh, founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and served as its president (~1804–1811).
